verified_against_binary: v2.37.2 completes the sweep begun in v2.37.1. Scanning every published prose string for six families of context assumption -- route/anaphora, page deixis, time-relative, release-relative, first person, reader-route -- returned mostly false positives (every 'the next' hit was 'the next session' or 'the next check', not document navigation; time-relative and first-person were empty) and five real defects of one kind: FACT-level prose pointing at its container. A fact renders in at least four places -- its topic page, the contract page, the Markdown twin, and facts.json, which has no pages at all -- so 'see this page's open question' resolves in one of them, and on the contract page it is actively wrong because all 52 rules sit together there. The contract page renders zero caveats, so that pointer was invisible exactly where it would have been most misleading. Fixed: delete.deny-set's caveat now states the unmeasured case instead of pointing at it; change.detect-at-use no longer says 'everything else on this page'; state.container-agent-range names the versions rather than a table; paths.session-paths-denied's withdrawal note says 'this rule' rather than 'this page'; and the plugins open question names the plugin-root rule instead of saying 'the rule on this page' where six rules sit. New validator rule applies to fact-level prose only -- page summaries, blurbs and open questions render in exactly one place, so 'this page' is correct there and is deliberately allowed, as is 'this site' everywhere. Checked against both real wordings plus three negative controls. No fact, tier, severity or date changed.
note: Found by a reader on a phone, not by any automated check -- the class had survived every prior pass because each instance reads perfectly well in isolation.
